title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, 1522 — RAH Salazar 9/23–9/26, DECODE R9593–R9657

steps.what: Searched for a prior decipherment; found Tomokiyo's article of 6 Sept 2025, which reconstructs the whole cipher from the contemporary decipherment attached to DECODE R9605. Saved to tomokiyo/.
Pulled DECODE record pages R9603-R9657 and tabulated the metadata (decode/getrec.py, decode/meta.py).

Checked the catalogue entry against the records: the run is 9/23-9/26 not 9/24, every record is dated 1522 so nothing reaches the July 1523 treaty, nine of the tail records are Lope Hurtado de Mendoza not Sánchez, and almost all carry a contemporary decipherment (DECODE 'Inline Cleartext: Yes').

Transcribed Tomokiyo's nomenclator to key_codes.tsv and tested its ordering: codes are C1(16) x V(5) x C3(9) and sorting by (C1, C3, V) puts the plaintext in alphabetical order, so unassigned codes are bracketed by their neighbours.
Fetched DECODE images for R9633-R9657, the 9/26 tail that Tomokiyo's article does not cover.
Predicted the unassigned numerals of the c-block by interpolation: cef=xxvi, cif=xxvii, cof=xxviii, cuf=xxix, cab/ceb/cib=xv/xvi/xvii.

Read the two-line foot cipher paragraph of R9653 f. 299r: 'cartas de Francia de xxvi y xxvii del passado de ...', which confirms the predicted cef=xxvi and cif=xxvii. Read the clear middle of the leaf (the siege of Rhodes) from the image.
Attempted the six-line head cipher paragraph of R9653 f. 299r; ink bleed from the facing leaf leaves it not confidently transcribable at the available resolution.

Checked whether the Lope Hurtado de Mendoza letters of the same group use Sánchez's cipher. R9648 f. 260v gives code groups ending in p and z (tep, tap, xulz), finals absent from Sánchez's third-position inventory {b c d f g h l m n}; so his key is a third member of the family, not Sánchez's. Whether it is Juan Manuel's is not settled.

Read R9635 f. 20r (16 Sept 1522, outside Tomokiyo's range) in part: a full page of cipher with a patchy interlinear decipherment. Recovered 'das cartas de vuestra magestad', 'los de esta republica', 'del senor infante', 'ducados allende de los otros xviii mil', 'mas de xv mil ducados', with the glosses 'obligados ... fuessen restituydas sus bienes'. Subject: sums owed by the Signoria under the capitulation and restitution of goods seized from imperial vassals.
cab = xv, predicted from the ordering rule, attested in 'ped xig cab pol9 vud+s' = 'mas de xv mil ducados'. Third of the seven predicted numerals confirmed in text; none contradicted.

Settled the notation: pol9 = pol (mi) + the letter sign for l = 'mil' (the l sign reads as a g in this hand); g-y + lal (publica) = 'republica'; the opening nulls are padded with the meaningless clear words 'como' and 'quien', which is what Tomokiyo's 'como quierr' note under the nulls column means.

Fetched R9605 (the record Tomokiyo broke the cipher from) and found its cipher and the clerk's full contemporary decipherment on facing leaves. Aligned the end of the letter: 'plegue adios nuf pac g-y-B-4-q-4 vog veg zn-B-ai nuf' = 'plegue a Dios no lo yerre en el camino', with vog veg = 'en el' met in situ.

Two findings from that alignment: code groups are used for syllables as well as whole words (nuf is 'no' the adverb and the last syllable of cami-no), so one-group-one-word segmentation fails; and the lookalike signs separate as B = m (camino), curly-q = r (ahora), bold-infinity = g, which is the largest source of error in reading the spelled runs at DECODE's resolution.

Attempted a continuous reading of the spelled-out letter runs on R9635 f. 20r. Not achieved: separating B / curly-q / bold-infinity is a judgement call at each occurrence and guessing them yields plausible Spanish that is not what the page says. Left marked rather than filled in; the R9605 calibration is the route through.

Continued the R9605 alignment: xel def = 'del visorey', ded+xof = 'venida', pog = 'mesmo', suf = 'hago', and the spelled run for 'escrivo' fixes z=c, curly-q=r, ai=i, m=v, #=o against ground truth. Correction to the published key: va = 'despacho', not Tomokiyo's 'desponho' (not a Spanish word), which also explains his puzzled 'me desponho x-e-r-o-n que' in R9623.

Checked whether the c-block numeral run starts where assumed, by aligning the group cud against the clear at 'que fue a ...'. Inconclusive: the date there is written over a correction and reads as two dates (xxv y xxvij), so it cannot be matched to one group. cab, cef and cif are unaffected, each having been confirmed in its own context.

Aligned the opening of R9605 (f. 39r) with the first page of its 1522 decipherment (f. 42), straight through: cig='ya', vu+x+e='dixe', vam+vuc+r='embaxador', spelled Hun-gria, sa='fue', r-e-s-p-o-n+di+do='respondido', de esta + r-e + publica = 'desta republica', xa + buen+a+s = 'con buenas'. Fixes the sign table against ground truth: n=a, y-curl=e, curly-q=r, ai=i, o=x, #=o, q=s, ao=p, &=n, m=v, z=c, B=m, plural=s. Note q=s here against Tomokiyo's alphabet q=t, two similar glyphs. Carried into alpha.py with the ground-truth values marked.

Applied the calibrated sign table to the first line of the unread R9635 f. 20r. It does not unlock it: deg, feb and z-n-r resolve to nothing, though the tail ('das cartas de vuestra magestad') and the null padding are secure. This corrects an earlier diagnosis in this folder - the bottleneck is not the sign table but the step before it, turning the cursive shapes into labels. R9605's hand and R9635's differ enough that a shape read as 'd' in one is something else in the other, and a wrong label yields a code group that does not exist or has the wrong value. The alignment must be done on the image, glyph against the clerk's word above it, not by transcribing to labels first.

Corrected the model of the writing, which was the real blocker: everything is written in ordinary latin-looking cursive, with three-letter trigrams as nomenclator codes and single letters/short runs as the substitution alphabet (n=a, y=e, g=r, o/x=x, #=o, ao=p, m=u/v, z=c, B=m, 9=l, q-double-bar=s). Verified on R9605 f. 39r l. 1 against the clerk's plaintext: cig vu-o-y n dom pud ho veg = 'Ya dixe a vuestra magestad que el'.

Edition pass on R9635 f. 20r (edition/r9635_f20r.md). ll. 2-3 read continuously: 'pues en esto no se puede perder nada ... con los de esta republica'. About a third of the page read; ll. 4-5, 8-13, 15-21, 23-25 left untranscribed rather than inferred.

New code value: lel = 'puede', bracketed between lal (publica) and lol (pudi) and fixed by sense in 'no se puede perder nada'. Also observed a code group used mid-word for a syllable (perder = p-e-r + xig(de) + r), the pattern R9605 showed with cami + nuf(no) = camino.

Edition pass continued on R9635 f. 20r: ll. 4, 9 and 10 added. l. 9 gives nul(obliga)+vuc(do)+s = 'obligados', which is exactly the word the 1522 decipherer wrote in the gloss above that stretch - key, alphabet and gloss agreeing independently. Coverage now about half the page; ll. 5, 8, 11-13, 15-21, 23-25 left untranscribed. The token gta, a dozen occurrences and not a possible code (middle position not a vowel), is left unresolved rather than forced.

Edition continued: ll. 9(right), 11 and 13 of R9635 f. 20r. 'me lo que antes de ahora'; yig(capitula)+c-i-o-n = 'capitulacion'; 'que quien Inglaterra que los' with hec = Inglaterra. Coverage now about three fifths of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15-21, 23-25 still untranscribed.

Edition continued: ll. 17-21 of R9635 f. 20r. 'estos xx mil de ahora'; 'poderlo hazer porque' with suf(ha)+z-e-r = hazer and lu(por)+ho(que) = porque; 'las quales' with lul(qual)+ta(es). Codes are also run together to make one word, the mirror of the stem-plus-ending pattern. Coverage about three quarters of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15, 16, 23-25 still untranscribed.

Edition continued: ll. 22-25 of R9635 f. 20r. 'darian todos los ...'; 'no pude de ... los'; 'si no se ... en'; and the page ends opening a fresh paragraph with the three nulls and 'los de esta republica'. cag is proposed as xxx (end of the numeral run, immediately before cig 'ya') but marked probable, not certain, being one slot past the attested run. Coverage about six sevenths of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15, 16 still untranscribed.

l. 5 of R9635 f. 20r: xof veg + p-r-i-m-e-r-o + xig ta = 'da el primero de es[te]', which fixes B = m on this page independently of 'camino' in R9605. At high zoom the ending of capitulacion on l. 11 is the curly second form of c that Tomokiyo draws as backwards-3, so capitulacion is settled rather than inferred. Coverage about nine tenths of f. 20r; ll. 8, 15, 16 remain.

Last lines of R9635 f. 20r: l. 15 = 'xviii mil ducados primer[o]', l. 13 'vuestra magestad', l. 16 'das las'. Every line of the page now has a reading of some kind; the page is read throughout in substance (subject, sums, parties, drift of the argument) while a scatter of spelled runs inside partially-read lines stays open. Recorded caveat: the crops were cut by dividing the written area into 25 equal bands, so line numbers are approximate and may be out by one; the readings are anchored to their own words, not to the numbering.

Moved to R9635 f. 21 (edition/r9635_f21.md): two more full pages of cipher, denser than f. 20r. The decipherer's gloss 'obligados ... fuessen restituydas sus tierras' continues here. A paragraph written entirely in the clear, marked A in the margin, reads in full: Richard Pace (Micer Ricardo Paceo), Henry VIII's envoy at Venice, has given Sanchez an enclosed memorial and asked him to press the Emperor for the letters Pace wants for the Pope and for don Juan (Juan Manuel at Rome); Sanchez seconds it. This fixes the identification behind the code hec = Inglaterra met on f. 20r. The two leaves are not yet transcribed line by line.

Grepped Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2 (1866; british-history.ac.uk pp380-519) by Salazar folio A.23-A.26 and 'Alonso Sanchez'. Fourteen of this folder's DECODE records are calendared as 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering' (nos. 429, 439, 444?, 447?, 462, 470, 473, 476, 482, 487, 488/489, 491, 495?, 500). R9635 = no. 476 (16 Sept 1522, A.26 ff. 20-22): the abstract confirms the 18,000 ducats outstanding and the Pace memorial, and shows the 'restituydas sus tierras' gloss is the Venetians' demand that their towns be restored. May 9/24 run and R9653 (20 Nov) not calendared.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Sánchez's 1522 cipher (cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm, 6 Sept 2025), checked against the clerk's full decipherment of R9605, was applied to R9635 and R9653, two letters outside Tomokiyo's coverage.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Not measurable: read_r9635.md and read_r9653.md list resolved code-group phrases only; the spelled-out letter runs are not transcribed, R9653's six-line head paragraph and ff. 21-22/300-301 are untranscribed, so no token base exists. Value from NOTES (share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked)
outcome.notes: The cipher itself was already solved and published by Tomokiyo in September 2025, so this is not a break. Added here: the catalogue entry's shelfmark, date range and authorship corrected; the ordering rule of the nomenclator, and from it a c-block numeral series of which cab = xv, cef = xxvi and cif = xxvii are confirmed in text and were not in the published key; and first readings of parts of R9635 and R9653, both outside Tomokiyo's coverage. fraction_read is the share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked; the spelled-out letter runs and the other 27 records are open. Also established that the nine Lope Hurtado de Mendoza records in the group are in a different cipher, which deserves its own target. The R9605 calibration fixes the sign values against ground truth but does not by itself unlock the unread pages: the binding constraint is the transcription of the cursive shapes, which differ between scribes, and that has to be done glyph by glyph on the image. An edition pass against the published key then began (edition/), reading about a third of R9635 f. 20r continuously and adding lel = 'puede' to the key.

gaps.item: R9635 f. 20r (about two thirds) and ff. 20v-22
gaps.detail: edition work against the published key; only ll. 1-3, 6, 7, 14, 22 done
ink bleed from the facing leaf at DECODE's resolution
most have a bound contemporary decipherment; transcription/edition not done

gaps.item: Lope Hurtado records R9634, R9644-R9646, R9648-R9650, R9652, R9656
gaps.detail: a third cipher, finals p/z absent from Sánchez's key; groups not in Tomokiyo's Juan Manuel table (see the lopehurtado1522 target)

prior.where: S. Tomokiyo, 'Correspondence in Cipher of Imperial Ambassadors Alonso Sanchez and Juan Manuel (1522)', https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm, posted 6 September 2025. Gives the substitution alphabet, ~177 code groups, and the deciphered opening lines of R9593-R9632. Also: English abstracts of 14 of these letters, made from the contemporary decipherings, in G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 429-500 (R9635 = no. 476); found 2026-09-21, after the partial reading of R9635.
